decode.content: Memory bandwidth can limit autoregressive token generation on a single consumer GPU because the process requires frequent data transfers between the GPU's memory and the computational units. As tokens are generated sequentially, the model must continuously read previous token information from memory and write new tokens to memory, leading to high memory access latency and demanding a high throughput of data. If the memory bandwidth is insufficient to keep up with the rate of data transfers, the GPU becomes a bottleneck, causing delays and reducing the overall efficiency of the token generation process.
